entry.title: DICE Awards named their GOTY, and I’m fairly certain you know who it is
entry.summary:
The 29th annual D.I.C.E. Awards have concluded, with the best games of 2025 selected in various categories. Of course, the Game of the Year award went to a title that has been dominating the award season since it started: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, but one title also got appreciation that it should've received during the TGA.
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 took home several D.I.C.E. awards aside from the ultimate one. It gained recognition in the Outstanding Achievement in Game Direction, Outstanding Achievement in Art Direction, and Outstanding Achievement in Story categories and received the RPG of the Year award to boot. It more or less swept the awards, even if it did lose out in some.
Expedition 33 utterly dominated the award season. Screenshot by Destructoid
A game that got the recognition it deserved to get at TGA (which was given to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 for no apparent reason) is Death Stranding 2: On the Beach. Kojima's cinematic "Strand-type" game received several awards from D.I.C.E., including Outstanding Technical Achievement and Outstanding Achievement in Audio Design. If it were up to me, that Game Direction award should've gone to Kojima as well due to the game's cinematics, cutscenes, and overall impressive and unique game design.
ARC Raiders got a bit of love as well, taking home the Online Game of the Year award. It came out a bit late in the release schedule, but it still managed to smash all expectations, getting recognized as an online powerhouse at just about every award show it got nominated in. Even we gave it an award for best live-service game, which it well deserved.
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 continues its award season dominance as it racks up award after award, no matter where and no matter from whom. If it gets nominated anywhere, chances are that it's going to win, and it's already set many records for accolades earned.

Overwatch, like all live-service games, can and will suffer from server issues from time to time.

How to check Overwatch server status
Mizuki (Support) | Image via Blizzard Entertainment
As of Feb. 14, Overwatch seems to be seeing some server instability, with players reporting difficulties getting into the game. Keep watch of the official Overwatch accounts, such as on X, to keep up to date with any potential server issues.
Overwatch currently has no official way of checking its server status, meaning you will have to resort to using third-party tools or checking in on Blizzard's official channels of communication to stay in touch with any potential server issues.
One tool is Downdetector, which shows user-reported errors. When they spike, chances are that the servers themselves are unstable or prone to disconnecting. Errors such as BN-564 can appear as well, which you can circumvent on Steam by doing a couple steps out of our dedicated guide. If you happen to encounter that error or any other, you can submit your own report to Downdetector to let others know.
Blizzard updates its players with news on server or connectivity issues on official accounts on platforms like X. As of Feb. 14, there haven't been official communications on any server outage, but that's still your best place to keep up with server status information.

entry.title: How to solve Ultrawide issue in REANIMAL
entry.summary:
REANIMAL's length of the main campaign might have earned some negative criticism, but the lack of official Ultrawide support is certainly a disappointment.
REANIMAL, so far, has been one of the better-made Unreal Engine 5 games that I have tested out. Unlike High on Life 2, the general performance is pretty good. That's until you try to run the game on an Ultrawide monitor. Thankfully, a mod has already appeared that allows you to bypass those limitations.
How to fix REANIMAL's Ultrawide issues
Since there's no official ultradwide support (yet) from Tarsier, the only option is to use a mod. You can download the mod files using this Codeberg link. You need to download the latest patch file. Click on the SUWSF Zip folder available under Installation.
This completes the first part of the task. Now, extract all the files that are within the SUWSF zip folder and store them in a separate folder. Copy all the files and paste them where the REANIMAL game is installed. The exact destination will be based on where you've installed it. For me, it's the common sub-folder within the Steam folder (where all my games on Steam download by default).
Made by Lyall, the mod adds third-party support for all ultrawide monitors. The additional support significantly improves the performance. There's also a chance for the mod to get updates in the future. While the hardware consumption actually goes up due to this mod, the general graphical performance felt smoother on my system.
How do you remove the mod? If you no longer want the mod for some reason, you simply have to delete the files. You can also open the SUWSF.ini file and set the Enabled command to false, but that's a far more complex method. The easier alternative is to delete the files and restart the game. If you want to use it again, just add the files to the game's installation folder, and you should have Ultrawide support for REANIMAL on your PC.

entry.title: How to complete the Good Ending achievement in High on Life 2
entry.summary:
High on Life 2 has plenty of achievements to complete, and the Good Ending is a secret one that you can finish pretty early in the game.
The name of the achievement might sound like 'the' good ending, but that's not the case. The achievement is named for what the game considers the 'right ending'. Let's look at how you can complete this achievement.
Disclaimer: Contains major story spoilers.
High on Life 2 Good Ending achievement guide
The earliest opportunity to complete the Good Ending achievement arrives right after the first mission. When it starts, you're declared a legendary bounty hunter. You also have a small museum that celebrates your previous achievements. Reach the bounty terminal, and Gene will announce that there's a huge bounty on your sister, Lizzie.
Image via Squanch Games
If you complete the quest as intended, you'll rescue Lizzie. Lizzie carries the Harper weapon, which was also present in the first game (as part of the DLC). In High on Life 2, she leads a rebel group and is considered a space terrorist. You can check out the bounty rewards and details on the bounty board.
When you meet Lizzie at the Aviary, fellow bounty hunters will surround her. However, they won't attack you at first. While I shot the other bounty hunters, you can instead shoot and kill Lizzie. While the game clearly wants you to eliminate the enemies, shooting Lizzie is a valid option.
Once you kill Lizzie, you'll complete the Good Ending achievement. However, the game immediately ends, and will cut to the end credits. You'll view a still image of Lizzie's funeral, followed by the notification of the achievement.
If you're opting for this ending, you'll once again need to start fresh and hunt the bounty hunters to continue the story.

entry.title: How to fast travel in High on Life 2
entry.summary:
High on Life 2 puts plenty of emphasis on exploration, and unlocking fast travel is going to save you plenty of time. Here's how you can do so.
Table of contents How to unlock fast travel in High on Life 2 How to use the fast travel feature in High on Life 2
How to unlock fast travel in High on Life 2
The very first mission in High on Life 2 involves reuniting with your sister, Lizzie. A part of the mission requires you to take down multiple enemies across several stages. Once you defeat Reptical for the second time (during the second fight, he will accept that he was wrong to hunt you down). You'll have to beat the timer to escape the lab with him.
At the end of the mission, you will lose consciousness as your suit shuts down. You'll then wake up at the Bleeding Star headquarters, with Lizzie and Gene by your side. At this point, you'll first get introduced to the Double-Jump unit.
Screenshot by Destructoid
Once the cutscene is over, head to Circuit Arcadia. Go to the tourist booth, and you'll be able to purchase a map for free. This unlocks the whole map and the fast travel feature.
How to use the fast travel feature in High on Life 2
First, open the map by pressing the M button. Then, pick a fast travel point on the map. A yellow icon denotes fast travel points, and you'll find several of them at key strategic points. These are called call stations, and you can interact with them for fast travel.
Once you interact, Gene will arrive with his RV. Jump inside, and you'll be able to fast travel to where you need to go.

entry.title: Best High on Life 2 graphics settings for no lag and max FPS
entry.summary:
High on Life 2 is now out on PC and consoles, and the general performance on the former platform is below par at best.
There have been instances of several players encountering occasional lags and stutters early on their adventures. The main culprit, once again, appears to be Unreal Engine 5. Thankfully, there are a few tweaks you can make on your own to smooth the performance.
Best High on Life 2 graphics settings
Before I deep dive into my current settings, here are the specifications of my PC.
AMD Ryzen 5600G
16 GB of DDR5 RAM
NVIDIA RTX 3060 12 GB
Here's the set of settings I have been using to get the best possible gameplay.
Window Mode: Windowed Fullscreen (depends completely on your personal preferences)
Resolution: 1920x1080 (depends on your setup)
Framerate Limit: 60
V Sync: Disabled
Graphics Quality: Medium
Upscaling: NVIDIA DLSS (FSR for AMD devices)
Upscaling Method: Balanced
Frame Generation Technologies: Off
Latency Reduction Technologies: Off
Motion Blur: Disabled
Chromatic Aberration: Disabled
FOV: 90
View Distance Quality: Medium
Global Illumination Quality: Medium
Anti-Aliasing Quality: Medium
Shadow Quality: Low
Post Process Quality: Medium
Texture Quality: Medium
Effects Quality: Medium
Foliage Quality: Reduce it to Low if you're struggling with performance
Image via Squanch Games
Here are some key pointers to remember. I have tried with unlimited FPS and 120 FPS. Both seem to cause trouble in the form of stutter. It could be my system, but I believe 60 FPS is a good limit if you have a weak hardware setup. While High on Life 2 is a shooter, it's not a competitive one. 60 FPS will be more than enough if you manage to keep the stutters away.
V-Sync comes disabled by default, and it's best to keep it that way. The extra feature doesn't offer much, but consumes a lot more resources.

entry.title: Reanimal review – the dollhouse horror of Little Nightmares gives way to a grimier tale of war and slaughter
entry.summary:
In an industry pestered by calls to "think of the children", Tarsier’s games are useful reminders that children can be utterly depraved in ways no coddling adult would ever dream. Later in Reanimal, the developer’s latest, strictly 'co-optional' horror game, two kids rip an eyeball out of a massive, sunken horse skull and shove it into what I sincerely hope is the eyesocket of a slumbering whale. Somehow, this is necessary to advance.
It’s the kind of thing that would only occur to children, because children do not reason like 'we' do, those disgusting creeps. They sense that they exist in a world that isn’t for them: a world of baffling laws, high shelves, and everyday monstrosity; a world they’re required to 'grow into' by means of repeated shedding and sprouting and subjection - milk teeth and pubic hair and doing your goddamn chores. So they instinctively come up with ways to screw with the system, twist its horrible logic against itself. Why not push a horse’s eyeball into a whale?

You’ll create a surface base from holographic modules, gather evidence about a doomed science expedition, research a wacky new element, and unearth the dirty secrets of your employer.

Yapyap stands apart from other “friendslop” horror extraction games by giving you plenty of firepower to begin with. Airpower, anyway. You and up to four mates are the boggle-eyed, flap-jawed minions of an enormous, moon-masked wizard. You’ve been summoned to wreak havoc on a rival wizard’s procedurally generated tower.
